Bytes proven; one slot (menu-appear_01) heard on a cold boot; every other slot's in-game cue is unproved.

input_constraints: Choose a slot by its catalogue slot id (nfl2k5ps2.audio.audo.o{outer:04d}.c{chunk:04d}) or, for the 154 disc-unique names, by name; raw offsets and filename guessing are never accepted, and the same slot may not be named twice in one run.

Input must be strict RIFF/WAVE integer PCM, 16-bit, whose chunks tile the file exactly with no metadata chunks, and whose channel count equals the slot's own (806 of 844 slots are mono, 38 stereo). A WAV at another rate is resampled to the slot's declared rate -- one of 11025, 22050, 16000, 14000, 20000, 12000, 15000 or 18000 Hz, per slot.

Fixed allocation, never longer: frames must fit the slot's own per-channel byte count (max_frames = per_channel_bytes // 16 * 28) and an over-length WAV is refused with the slot's exact capacity in seconds rather than truncated. This writer never grows a slot; all 153 adjacent AUDO pairs inside an entry have gap 0, so there is no inter-chunk slack to borrow.

The encoded blocks are followed by silent filler to the declared byte count and LOOP_END|LOOP is set on the last real block, so the SPU stops before the filler; the descriptor and the 0x20 wrapper are never rewritten.
Stereo is written as two contiguous per-channel halves, L then R -- not the channel-major interleave the Xbox row uses. Proved on 38 of 38 stereo chunks by the per-half LOOP_END position.
A payload that would cross a 1 GiB pack seam is refused. No AUDO does (0 of 844); the guard exists because 2 of the 17 AUSB stream banks do, and AUSB is a separate row.

The source ISO is opened read-only and re-hashed after the run; the destination is created with O_EXCL so a run cannot overwrite an existing image or land on the image it read, and every refusal leaves no output image behind.

690 of 844 chunks share a name with another chunk (161 distinct names across 844 chunks; two crowd sounds occupy 340 chunks each). The physical span is exact but the in-game cue is not proved, so a UI must warn that replacing one slot may change an unexpected or duplicate-sounding cue.

In the PS2 Disc Studio this lane is one tab: every refusal above is shown inline or at Check before an image exists, and the build writes a new image only after the lane's independent verifier passes.

input_constraints: Shorter or equal, never longer: across all 6,873 strings an allocation is exactly len(text) * 2 + 2 bytes, so there is zero slack anywhere on the disc and the character budget is the original string's own length. One code unit longer is refused, and the refusal states the budget.

Scope is the five banks and nothing else: franchise, credits, situation and trivia text. The in-game HUD and play-call strings (CHOOSE PACKAGE, COACH'S PICK, penalty banners) are in none of the disc's 716 text banks — measured on six save-state screens, 0 of 6,873 catalogued strings — so this row cannot change them.

Only the 6,658 editable strings may be written. A string is editable only when its whole resource body rebuilds byte-identically from the decoded structure, its allocation is a NUL-terminated UTF-16LE run on a pool-entry boundary, it has room for at least one code unit past its terminator, and its consumer is display copy rather than lookup: 50 SITU scenario selectors and 165 zero-capacity CRED/STRG allocations stay read-only.
Inline tokens are preserved exactly: dropping, adding or reordering a pipe-delimited marker from the 57-entry token table is refused, because the engine draws a glyph where the marker sits.

An LZ-compressed bank is refused outright rather than recompressed -- no text bank on the retail disc is compressed (chunk magic 0), so wiring in the refit layer would add the hazard that hung an attract demo without buying anything.
A bank that straddles two pack files is refused: one bounded ISO9660 file replacement cannot cover it. All five in-scope banks live entirely inside /VC_20919/0.
A bank this disc does not decode as UTF-16LE is refused rather than guessed at, and two recipe edits may not target the same allocation or overlapping allocations.
An optional expect_sha256 per edit pins the original string's digest, so a recipe written against a different disc or index is refused before anything is created.

Aliasing is reported, never hidden: 281 allocations are referenced by more than one lookup record, 279 of them editable and the most-shared editable one by 18 records, so a UI must show 'used by N records' rather than pretending aliases are independent strings.
The source image is opened read-only and re-hashed; the destination is created with O_EXCL and must not already exist.

A created formation or play is a clone of a donor plus authored slot positions and node chains; the group bits on a formation-to-play menu link stay unproved, so the writer only ever reuses a value the book already uses.

One pack per run. Every PLAY resource lives in /VC_20919/0., so this has never bound, but the guard stays rather than being assumed away.

The PLAY chunks are uncompressed on all 37 books, so there is no decode on read and no recompression on write; a compressed family would need a re-encoder that fits the old size and this writer does not have one.
An unknown book id or a recipe with the wrong schema is refused, and the source ISO is opened read-only while the destination is created with O_EXCL and must not already exist.

gui.reason: Surfaces as the Stadium tab of the PS2 Disc Studio (File ▸ PS2 Disc Studio…, or --ps2-disc-studio), the separate PS2 window that follows the save editor and the Disc Inventory: targets come from this lane's catalogue tool run over the user's own disc, the budget is on screen, refusals are inline, the patcher's dry run happens before any image exists, the build writes a NEW image, and the lane's independent verifier gives the verdict. input_constraints: Positions only, same count: vertex count comes from the pinned catalogue row rather than the recipe, and a mismatch is refused -- on PS2 the count is a VIF NUM field, so changing it is a topology change.

Only catalogued position lanes may change. Every other byte is the user's: the V4_16 header block, the V4_5 colour and V2_16 UV unpacks, the DMA tags, the VU1 microprogram invocation and every w component are preserved bit-exact, and the verifier requires the whole 0x20 resource wrapper to be byte-identical.

Fixed allocation at three nested levels: the ISO extent keeps its length, the rebuilt chunk span is byte-for-byte the size of the old one so no successor chunk moves and no outer entry changes, and the VC-LZ body must fit stored_size with the wrapper's in-place-decode scratch word left at its retail value. Raising that word is what hung an attract demo, so this writer never does.

A recompression that does not fit is refused before the destination image is created. The retail packer left 0 to 16 spare bytes per scene (median 8), so a retail-identical encoder has no room at all: the writer runs greedy first, falls back to an optimal parse, then expands trailing matches back into literals so the body still fills stored_size exactly.
Encoder geometry is taken from the source stream rather than assumed -- the scenes use both offset_bits 12 and 13.
A coordinate that is not an exact binary32 is refused, as is an unauthorised target, a catalogue pin that does not match, and a recipe whose edits span two scenes.

Aliased lanes are refused: several batch descriptors can point at the same DMA chain, so of 1,041 catalogued targets there are 890 distinct payload spans and 274 targets share a span with another. Each row carries its payload_span_target_count and a recipe editing two aliases of one lane is rejected -- the first real-disc trial run was refused by exactly that check.
The source ISO is opened read-only and its digest re-checked afterwards; the destination is created with O_EXCL and must not already exist.
The 8 batches on the trial scene whose VIF command 0x3F is unknown are excluded rather than guessed at; coverage there is 646 of 654 batches.

In the PS2 Disc Studio this lane is one tab: every refusal above is shown inline or at Check before an image exists, and the build writes a new image only after the lane's independent verifier passes.

runtime.scope: Offline only: bytes proven, pixels not; nothing has been booted, and every runtime_visibility_proved and hardware_visibility_proved flag in the outputs is false. What is proved offline is the shape/batch/DMA/VIF layout against the retail disc -- corroborated independently by all 23,075 decoded vertices lying inside their own shape's declared bounding sphere, maximum distance-over-radius exactly 1.000000 with 242 of 1,041 lanes past 0.999 -- plus a same-count position edit round-tripping through decode, edit, recompression into the fixed span, ISO9660 write and independent verification. The real-disc trial moved 250 vertices (the five distinct position lanes of one sideline shape, +400 on y) in outer entry 1556 chunk 2: 1,000 decoded bytes changed in 250 one-vertex runs; the recompressed body fit only through the optimal parse, because the retail packer had left 3 spare bytes (10,303 literal-fill bytes, 8 bytes padding, scratch word unchanged); 1,282,669 image bytes changed, all inside the single declared window, with the 0x20 wrapper and the 9-byte VC-LZ header untouched; the lane verifier and the ISO9660 verifier both passed and the source image re-hashed unchanged. A runtime witness would be booting the patched image in PenguinScreen2/PCSX2 and seeing the moved geometry -- which would also be the first time a console decoder has been watched consuming an optimal-parse VC-LZ stream rather than a retail one.

gui.reason: The exporter writes only the uniform targets the open Xbox project marks edited, naming each file by the PS2 texture's PCSX2 replacement identity from the shipped manifest (TEX0 and CLUT XXH3-64 hashes computed offline from the stock disc; 4,732 names resolve to exactly one Xbox asset). It never emits an unedited texture, never touches the user's ISO, and publishes into a fresh folder with a receipt. The independent verifier re-derives from folder + receipt + manifest, importing none of the exporter. It is a separate window (File menu, or --ps2-export) in the shape of the PS2 disc inventory and save editor, not a card in the Xbox sidebar. Before exporting, the window asks where the pack will be used (three answers, nothing preselected, Export disabled until one is chosen) and explains the emulator naming history on hover; that explanation is a validated contract, not decoration. It is also reachable from the PS2 Disc Studio's PCSX2 Pack page, which opens this same window on a saved .2k5mod the user chooses (that window has no Xbox session) and afterwards offers tools/nfl2k5_ps2_replacement_pack_kit.py to write that emulator's kit beside the pack; no disc image is read and no ISO is written by that path.

input_constraints: Only edited targets are eligible: an uniform target without user-authored PNG bytes in the open project is never written, because an unedited texture would be retail pixels leaving the disc.

Names come from the shipped manifest only (schema nfl2k5_ps2_to_xbox_texture_map/v1); a target with no manifest row, or an ambiguous one, is reported as skipped with its reason and nothing is written for it.

The output folder must not already exist and may not be a symlink; files are written to a temporary sibling and published by rename, and the folder contains only textures/SLUS-20919/replacements/*.png plus the receipt.
Where the PS2 native geometry (TW/TH decoded from the name's bits word) differs in aspect from the user's PNG, the image is resampled to the PS2 aspect and the resample is recorded in the receipt.

The export asks where the pack will be used and has no default: PenguinScreen2 with Classic Texture Names on (recommended: whole-texture hashing restored, every file loads), PCSX2 1.7.4034 or newer including 2.x (loads these names; textures a game draws clamped would be skipped, and none of this manifest's names fell in that class across the 60 dumps measured), or PCSX2 before 1.7.4034. The answer is recorded in the receipt as emulator_target with the settings that target needs; LoadTextureReplacements=true is needed in every case; the files written are identical for every answer.

Each answer carries a hover tooltip and an identical accessible description explaining the PCSX2 1.7.4034 region-hash change, the 1.7.5606 TCC-flag change and what Classic Texture Names restores. The text is one constant (TARGET_EXPLANATION_REQUIRED_FACTS, 13 measured facts) and bash tools/validate_nfl2k5_ps2_replacement_pack.sh prints NFL2K5_PS2_EXPORT_TARGET_EXPLANATION_PASS only while every fact is still present.
